findings.title: include_website_name lacks `?`, so website_name leaks for TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers
findings.body:
ActiveModel::Serializers only honours filter methods named `include_<attr>?`. The method here is `include_website_name` with no question mark, so it is never consulted and `website_name` is always serialized.

On top of that, `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. For a TL0 user viewed anonymously, `website` is hidden by `restrict_user_fields?`, but `website_name` still exposes the website host and, for same-domain sites, the full path. That defeats the anti-spam restriction on untrusted profile fields.

Fix: rename the method to `include_website_name?` and make it apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` check, e.g. by adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

findings.title: Untrusted-attribute spec does not cover the new website_name field
findings.body:
The TL0/anonymous spec checks that untrusted attributes are absent, but its list does not include `website_name`. As a result, the leak of the website host and path to anonymous viewers goes untested.

The new specs also never exercise the sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) or the `website_host.nil?` path.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains under multi-part TLDs as the same site
findings.body:
The sibling branch decides two hosts belong to the same site by stripping only the first label from each and comparing the rest. Unrelated sites under multi-part public suffixes therefore match: `foo.co.uk` vs `bar.co.uk` compares `co.uk == co.uk` and shows the full URL path. Likewise `a.github.io` vs `b.github.io` would match.

The display is then inconsistent with the intent of only showing the full path for the instance's own domain.
